verdict.rationale: Windmill documents workspace-level Variables and secrets stored centrally and encrypted with a workspace-specific key. It also documents a general roles and permissions system for controlling access within workspaces. The evidence does not show per-credential sharing or ACLs controlling who can use which credential, and token scoping concerns API tokens, not stored credentials. missing for 10: explicit documentation of sharing individual credentials/resources with team members or groups, per-credential usage permissions, a dedicated connection-credential (resource) type, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can store connection credentials centrally, share them with my team, and control who can use which credential

citations.quote: All Variables (not just secrets) are encrypted with a workspace specific symmetric key to avoid leakage.
Windmill provides a roles and permissions system that allows you to control access and manage permissions within your instance and workspaces.
